text:
B: Alright, mate! Can you hear me? Rhys.
A: Yeah, loud and clear. Tomasz. How's it going?
B: Not bad, not bad. Bit knackered, I was up at half four for work, so I'm running on energy drinks and vibes, to be honest.
A: Half four. What do you do, bakery?
B: Nah, supermarket. Shelf stacking, early shift. Replenishment, if you want the posh word.
A: Okay. Supermarket.
B: What about you? You look like you're in sales or something, you've got that look, like.
A: Ha, good guess. Yeah, cars. Premium German, dealership in west London. Saturday I sold three.
B: Three? In one day? That's mad. What's that, like, commission and that?
A: Basic plus commission. Good month, it's very good money. Bad month, you eat pasta.
B: I eat pasta every month, mate.
A: Ha. Yeah.
B: I've been thinking about doing personal training, actually. Or plastering. One of the two. You look like you go gym, do you?
A: Four mornings a week. Bench is hundred and twenty.
B: Hundred and twenty! I think I'd struggle with the bar on its own, honestly. I keep saying I'll start running, but then it's Wednesday, five-a-side, and I'm blowing after ten minutes.
A: Personal trainer, you need to look the part, mate. Nobody pays someone who's out of breath. You need to train first, properly, six months, then do the course. Otherwise is waste of money.
B: Yeah, no, that's fair, to be fair. Six months. I'll start Monday.
A: Everybody starts Monday.
B: Ha! True. Where you from originally? Your accent, like.
A: Poland. Wrocław. London sixteen years now.
B: Oh, tidy. Wales played Poland a while back, didn't they. You was probably happy with that one.
A: Maybe. I don't remember, honestly. I watch Arsenal mostly, and Śląsk Wrocław.
B: Cardiff for me. It's pain, mate. Pure pain. Have you ever been to Cardiff?
A: No. Never been to Wales.
B: You've got to come for the Six Nations, honestly. Whole city goes mental, pubs are rammed, everyone singing. Me and the boys go every year, we start at like eleven in the morning and I don't remember the second half, do you know what I mean. It's the best weekend of the year.
A: Rugby is not really my thing.
B: Fair. What about holidays, then? Where d'you go?
A: Dubai last year. Marbella, Lisbon. Nice hotel, pool on the roof.
B: Oh, unreal. I've done Magaluf and Benidorm. Not quite rooftop pool, like.
A: Different budget.
B: Ha, yeah. Bit. My passport's running out anyway, I need to sort that—
A: So, the puzzle. You finished?
